title: Scene Template (design-time)
description: Addendum section 3, Stage A. One template per (channel, semantic strategy). A template is a STATIC placeholder: it fixes the environment, the objects and where they sit, the camera path, the typography layout and timing, and the transitions. Only the `parameters` it declares may vary at runtime, and only with data extracted from the script. Section 3 is explicit that the runtime engine may not decide any of this -- it may only select a template and fill it. A strategy with no template for a channel is a hard abort, never a fallback.

strategy.description: The semantic strategy this template serves, e.g. ACCUMULATION. Must exist in visual/strategies.js.

name.description: Stable identifier. The runtime plan names this verbatim under TEMPLATE SELECTED, so it must never be renamed once a plan has referenced it.

intent.description: What the viewer is meant to understand from this template, in one sentence. Not rendered; it is the thing a reviewer checks the template against.

environment.description: Section 8 forbids a single shared staging system. Each template stages itself, and `type` must equal the channel's declared environment_type -- the validator enforces that.

ground.description: What the objects rest on or sit within, in this template's own words: 'a matte desk surface', 'a printed page', 'terrain seen from orbit'.

objects.description: Every object drawn by this template, with where it sits. Each `object` must be one of the channel's core_objects -- that is what stops a template inventing a visual world its channel never declared.

role.description: Exactly one object must be the subject.

anchor.description: Fraction of the frame, 0..1. The renderer resolves these against the safe rect; it does not reposition them.

repeats.description: Name of a `parameters` entry. A `list` parameter draws the object once per item. A `number` parameter draws that many copies, capped by its `max_items` — which is how ACCUMULATION accumulates, because the strategy's own dataNeeds is `total`, a number, not an enumeration. A count-driven repeat must also set `repeat_note`.

repeat_note.description: Required when `repeats` points at a `number`. States plainly whether the count is quantitative (N objects means N things) or symbolic (N objects stand for a total). Printed verbatim in the plan, so a symbolic pile can never be read as a data claim.

camera_path.description: Ordered keyframes. Every `move` must appear in the channel's camera_language; a move the channel did not declare is a validator failure, which is section 8's 'no generic camera rig' made enforceable.

target.description: Which object the move is toward, if any.

reason.description: Why the camera does this here. A move with no reason is decoration.

typography.description: Every piece of on-screen text. Empty is legal and often correct: section 8 prefers physical representation over numeric display. `face` must be one of the channel's two declared families and `placement` its declared text_placement.

slot.description: Either a literal string, or `{param}` naming a `parameters` entry.

is_primary_visual.description: Section 8: a numerical display may only be the primary visual element where the template explicitly supports it. Setting this true is that explicit support, and the validator demands a `justification`.

transitions.description: Transitions out of this scene. Each must be in the channel's transition_language.

to.description: `next` for the following beat, or a template name.

parameters.description: The only things runtime may vary. Each declares its type and where it must come from; the plan generator refuses to fill one from anywhere else.

from.description: Which extractor supplies it. Nothing may be filled from general knowledge.
